newsitem.title: USA: Bell Atlantic to invest $5 bln in wireline network.
newsitem.headline: Bell Atlantic to invest $5 bln in wireline network.

text.p: Bell Atlantic, whose $25.6 billion merger with Nynex Corp was approved on Thursday, said Friday it expects to invest about $5 billion in 1997 to maintain quality and add to its U.S. wireline activity.
The company also said it aims to capture at least 25 percent of the long distance market in its region during the next five years.

In a written statement marking the completion of its merger, Bell Atlantic said it will offer in-region long distance service "as soon as possible." It said in-region and long distance is a $20 billion opportunity for the combined company.

The Federal Communications Commission on Thursday approved the merger of Bell Atlantic Corp. and Nynex. The merger forms the nation's largest local carrier and the number two phone company after long distance giant AT&T Corp.

Ivan Seidenberg, Bell Atlantic's vice president and chief operating officer, will become chief executive of the new company by August 1998, and chairman upon the retirement at the end of 1998 of current chairman and CEO Raymond Smith.

Bell Atlantic also said it remains authorized under a current program to repurchase up to about 10 million shares by December 31. It said it will buy back no more than about 35 million shares during the two years following the merger, since it will follow pooling-of-interest accounting rules.
